text: The ghee roast dosa is exactly what the name promises: crackling, glossy, and the chutney trio is fresh. Pongal was a little salty but I would come back for the dosa alone.
Best Mysore masala dosa in Jayanagar right now. The red chutney actually has heat. Filter coffee is strong and not too sweet.
Podi idli is addictive. Benne masala dosa was good but not as buttery as Davanagere. Crowded at 8am on Sundays, expect to stand.
Thatte idli is soft as anything, sambar tastes like home. My parents loved it.
Dosa was great, bisi bele bath was lukewarm and the boondi had gone soft. Service rushed us out.
Medu vada are properly crisp. Coffee could be hotter. Still my go-to before work.
Rava idli with the sagu is a proper Malleshwaram breakfast. Kesari bath ran out by 9:40 though.
Khara bath plus kesari bath (chow chow) for 115 rupees. Unbeatable. Neer dosa was surprisingly good for a darshini.
Masala dosa was average, the potato palya lacked salt. Maddur vada was crisp and lovely though.
Mangalore buns are the reason I come. Badam milk is too sweet for me.
Set dosa is spongy and soaks up the sagu well. Standing tables only, so not for long chats.
Kesari bath with pineapple and plenty of ghee. Nothing fancy, everything right.
Proper wedding-style oota. The Mysore saaru is the highlight, nice and peppery. Wish the palya had more variety.
Unlimited banana leaf meal and they keep coming back with ghee. Obbattu was soft and warm. Go hungry.
Akki rotti with dill is excellent. Majjige huli was a bit thin.
Ragi mudde was fine but the soppu saaru was too salty on my visit. Long wait on a Sunday.
Paal payasa tastes like my grandmother's. The mini thali is perfect on weekdays.
Chitranna and kosambari are fresh and bright. Good place to take visitors from out of state.
Mutton donne biryani is the best in Koramangala. Meat falls off the bone, the green masala has real chilli kick. Brinjal gravy is a must.
Chicken donne biryani has that seeraga samba aroma. Chicken kebab is properly red and crisp.
Biryani is great but the mutton pepper fry was too chewy on my visit. Phirni was a nice finish.
Egg biryani is underrated, and good value. Weekend wait was 35 minutes.
Veg biryani is just okay, feels like an afterthought. Gobi 65 was good.
Ordered three mutton biryanis for the office. Everyone went silent. Enough said.
Consistent and fast. Chicken kebab could use more curry leaves but the biryani never disappoints.
The Andhra veg meal is fierce in the best way. Gunpowder ghee rice is dangerously good. Gutti vankaya was too oily though.
Gongura mutton is the real thing, sour and fiery. Ask for extra ghee with the podi.
Kodi kura made me cry a little. In a good way. Bring a lassi from next door.
Pesarattu upma is a great lunch, light but filling. Pootharekulu to finish is a nice touch.
Way too spicy for me even after asking for mild. Chilli paneer pulao was a chilli bomb. Staff were friendly though.
Meals come fast and they refill rasam without asking. Gongura pickle on the cart is excellent.
Degree coffee in a brass dabarah, done properly. Ghee podi dosa is a perfect pairing. My favourite morning spot.
Iced filter coffee tonic sounds odd but works. Banana bread was a bit dry.
Rava kesari cheesecake is genius. Coffee is the best in Indiranagar.
Idli sambar bowl is comforting. Laptop crowd takes the back room by noon.
Cappuccino was fine but overpriced next to the filter coffee. Vada pav was cold.
Coconut cookie is vegan and crunchy. Nice that they mark vegan items clearly.
Butter chicken is good but sweet for my taste and the tandoori chicken was a bit dry. Pricey for what it is.
Dal makhani is the best I have had in Bengaluru, smoky and deep. Garlic naan arrived blistered and hot.
Rogan josh is properly rich. Laccha paratha is flaky. Service a bit slow on Friday.
Malai broccoli converted my broccoli-hating husband. Shahi tukda is decadent.
Butter chicken is excellent, paneer lababdar a little too sweet.
Great for a big group dinner. Ask for the corner table.
Kadai paneer is smoky, with real wok hei. Tandoori roti was perfect. Exactly what Whitefield needed.
Chole was good but the Amritsari kulcha was doughy inside. Lassi is great.
Dhaba chicken curry with roti is a solid post-work dinner. Loud, cheerful place.
Sarson ka saag with white butter is seasonal and worth it. Paneer tikka was nicely charred.
Egg bhurji pav was too oily. Service was slow even when it was empty.
Good chicken curry, generous portions. Not fine dining, does not pretend to be.
Seekh kebab is the best on Mosque Road and that is saying something. Smoked chicken tikka is juicy with real charcoal flavour.
Galouti melts. Sheermal with nihari on a Friday is a religious experience.
Boti kebab was smoky and tender. Biryani is decent, not their strength.
Came during Ramzan, worth the chaos. Kaddu ki kheer is lovely and not too sweet.
Hara bhara kebab was bland and the vegetarian options are limited. Meat eaters will love it.
Opens only at 4 but worth planning around. Parking is a nightmare.
Nihari is rich, sticky and slow. Bring friends, order everything.
Kori rotti is exactly like in Mangaluru. Prawn ghee roast is fiery and glossy.
Fish gassi with neer dosa is comforting. Pomfret was a little overfried.
Mushroom ghee roast for the vegetarians is a smart touch, really good. Sol kadhi is refreshing.
Squid sukka with kudampuli is perfect. Elaneer payasam to end. Will be back.
Prices have gone up a lot. Prawn ghee roast portion was small for 560.
Kadle manoli is a nice vegan side. Calm place for a weekday lunch.
Finally a vegan margherita where the cashew mozzarella actually melts. The vegan tiramisu is creamy and not cloying. Instant favourite.
Margherita was fine, but nothing on the menu has any spice and it is expensive for what you get. Not for me.
Cacio e pepe is textbook. Dough on the pizza is leopard-spotted and chewy.
Burrata is fresh, diavola had a nice chilli honey kick. Weekend wait was long.
Pesto genovese vegan is bright and fresh. Truffle funghi pizza for the non-vegans was a hit too.
Great pizza, small portions of pasta. Ask for the window seat to watch them roll it.
Tiramisu della casa deserves its reputation. Carbonara is the real thing, no cream.
Pumpkin ravioli with sage butter is lovely. Bruschetta trio was good, not great.
Spaghetti pomodoro is vegan and simple, but they had nothing vegan for dessert. Pretty lakeside setting.
Lasagne is rich and generous. Service attentive but slow.
Minestrone was watery. Panna cotta with jamun compote is a fun twist.
Romantic outdoor seating, a good tiramisu, a slightly salty carbonara.
The cardamom bun is worth the queue. Croissant is honeycombed and buttery. Pour-over had a lovely jaggery note.
Flat white is consistent. Almond croissant a bit too sweet for me.
Eggs on sourdough are silky. Best brunch in 7th block.
Pour-over is excellent and black coffee is vegan, but almost all the bakes have butter or egg. Wish there were vegan pastries.
Lemon tart is properly sharp. Mushroom toast is generous.
Iced mocha was too sweet and the place is loud at noon. Bakes are great though.
Avocado toast was fine but underseasoned. The cold brew tonic was the best thing I had. Lovely plants, slow service.
Big brunch plate on a Sunday, perfect hangover cure. Iced filter coffee is a great idea.
Shakshuka is well spiced, pita a bit cold. Nice place to work from.
Açaí bowl is fresh and not too sweet. Banoffee jar is dessert heaven.
Chicken pesto sandwich was dry. Coffee saves it.
Grilled veg pasta was light and good. Quiet on weekdays.
Momos were okay but the chicken filling was bland and the place is tiny. Not worth the hype for me.
Jhol momos are incredible, the sesame-tomato broth is addictive. Sepen sauce is lethal.
Thukpa on a rainy evening. Perfect. Pan-fried paneer momos are crisp and creamy.
Veg momos are fresh with lots of ginger. Chilli potato is great with a beer.
Shapale is crisp and juicy. Butter tea is an acquired taste but I acquired it.
Thenthuk is hearty and vegan. Small place, expect to share a table.
Consistently good momos for under 200. Jhol is the move.
Tonkotsu broth is milky and deep, the egg is jammy. Best ramen in the city.
White miso vegan ramen is creamy and comforting, a rare good vegan ramen. A bit salty.
Tantanmen is spicy and nutty. Karaage was crisp but small.
Shoyu ramen was underwhelming, broth too light. Counter seating is cramped.
Agedashi tofu is delicate and lovely. Matcha mochi to finish.
Great ramen, slow service when full. Go before 7.
Pork belly bao is sticky and rich. Kung pao has real Sichuan tingle.
Thai green curry (veg) is fresh and fragrant. Lychee iced tea is great.
Dan dan noodles were oily. Crispy tofu bao was good.
Plenty of vegan options, clearly marked. Sushi bowl was fresh but a bit plain.
Basil fried rice is a solid weekday lunch. Whitefield needed this.
Red curry was too sweet for me. Nice interiors.
Double smash has those crispy lace edges. Fries are excellent. Shake was too sweet.
Nashville hot chicken burger is properly hot and crunchy. Best burger in Koramangala.
BBQ bacon burger with onion rings is outrageous. Loud music, great vibe.
Crispy paneer burger is legit, not a sad veg option. Buffalo wings are tangy.
Beyond smash is a great vegan burger, the bun is vegan too. Fries are vegan. Loud though.
Loaded cheese fries are a meal. Late-night open is a blessing.
Smash burger every Friday. Never miss.
Gongura chicken burger is a brilliant idea, tangy and spicy. Mango thokku fries too.
Classic cheeseburger was overcooked. Paneer tikka burger is the better choice.
Filter coffee shake is genius. Aloo tikki burger is a good cheap lunch.
Chicken popcorn was soggy by the time it arrived. Rose falooda shake was nice.
Masala onion rings are a great snack. Fun menu.
Good, cheap, creative. Not life-changing.
Masala puri like the old Gandhi Bazaar carts, hot peas gravy and loads of sev. Mirchi bajji is properly spicy.
Pani puri water has a real kick. Samosa chaat is huge.
Dahi puri balanced perfectly between sweet and tangy. Cheap and brilliant.
Samosas fried in front of you. Kulfi falooda to cool down.
Pav bhaji had too much butter even for me, and it is chaotic at 7pm.
Best evening snack stop in Basavanagudi. Hygiene is better than the carts.
Cheese chilli paddu is fun and actually spicy. The green chutney is so good I bought the jar.
Ragi paddu is crisp and healthy-ish. Idli vada combo is standard.
Plain paddu was a bit dense. Open butter masala dosa was great though.
Sweet banana appe is a lovely end. Kids love this place.
Lemon sevai was dry and the masala paddu came cold. Chutney is still top.
Paddu with chutney and coffee is a perfect cheap breakfast.
Three saarus on one thali. Pepper rasam clears the sinuses. Naati koli saaru on Sunday is outstanding.
Andhra thali is hot and generous. Ulavacharu is smoky and unusual.
Bassaru with ragi mudde is real home food. Curd rice with pomegranate is a nice touch.
Mutton chops were tough. Kayi holige was good.
Simple, honest thali. Service is quick and kind.
Pepper rasam in a glass is a great idea. Rajajinagar regulars know.
Vegan chocolate torte is rich and fudgy, and the vegan mango panna cotta is fresh. Wish there were more vegan cupcakes.
Jaggery coconut cheesecake is unique and delicious. Tres leches soaked perfectly.
Red velvet cupcake is moist. Hot chocolate is thick.
Eggless chocolate cupcake is the best eggless cake I have had.
Gulab jamun cheesecake jar was too sweet. Nice idea though.
Great dessert stop after dinner in Whitefield.
Tofu scramble that actually tastes of something. Vegan mushroom risotto is creamy without any dairy. The glasshouse in morning light is gorgeous.
Buddha bowl is fresh and filling. Pricey for a bowl.
Vegan berry cheesecake fooled my non-vegan friend. Oat latte is good.
Eggs Benedict for the non-vegans is excellent too. Lovely light.
Vegan pesto pizza base was soggy. Service was slow.
My go-to for clean, tasty food. Green juice every Saturday.
